note: Fact corrections to the v3 snapshot. scripts/port-legacy.mjs applies every edit to the source text before converting and FAILS when a 'find' string is no longer in the page (the snapshot moved: re-check the fact, then update or drop the row). Each page with a correction carries its note as a callout at the top. Only verified facts go here, each with its evidence.

pages.evidence: despia-framework proof/v3-v4-parity/DOCS-NOTE-store-location.md: V3 iOS reads SKPaymentQueue.default().storefront.countryCode (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, 'USA' on the parity simulators); V3 Android reads Play Billing BillingConfig.getCountryCode() (alpha-2, 'US').
pages.callout: Corrected on 8 October 2026: iOS returns a three-letter code (`USA`, `DEU`, `JPN`) and Android a two-letter code (`US`, `DE`, `JP`). This page used to say both return `US`, so an iOS check against `'US'` never matched. The examples below compare against the right value.

edits.find: A user in Spain signed into a US App Store account returns `US`.
edits.replace: A user in Spain signed into a US App Store account returns `USA` on iOS (`US` on Android).

edits.find: It returns a two-letter ISO country code like `US`, `DE`, `JP`, or `BR`.
edits.replace: It returns the store's own country code: a three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code on iOS (`USA`, `DEU`, `JPN`, `BRA`) and a two-letter alpha-2 code on Android (`US`, `DE`, `JP`, `BR`). Normalize before comparing if you support both platforms.

edits.replace: iOS reports three-letter codes (`USA`) and Android two-letter codes (`US`), so normalize to one form first.

pages.callout: Corrected on 8 October 2026: `despia.storeLocation` is `USA` on iOS and `US` on Android. The web payment check below is for iOS users of the US App Store, so it compares against `'USA'`; see [Store Location](/native-features/store-location) for the full platform gate.
